documents.title: Press release: Veritas Analytics acquires Dunmore Data
documents.text:
MILAN – Veritas Analytics, a provider of business intelligence software, announced on Tuesday that it has agreed to acquire Dunmore Data, a Dublin-based start-up specializing in the analysis of customer feedback. The transaction, whose value was not disclosed, is expected to close in the first quarter of next year, subject to regulatory approval.

Dunmore Data, founded six years ago by two former university researchers, employs forty-five people and counts several European retailers among its clients. Its software, which can classify thousands of customer comments within minutes, will be integrated into Veritas's existing platform and offered to its 2,300 corporate customers. "Our clients have told us that they are drowning in unstructured feedback," said Veritas chief executive Silvia Romano. "Dunmore's technology turns it into decisions."

Veritas said that all Dunmore employees will be offered positions, and that the Dublin office will remain open and become the company's European center for language technology. The founders, Dr. Aoife Brennan and Dr. Callum Reid, will stay for at least two years to oversee the integration. Analysts have welcomed the deal but note that integrating a small, research-driven team into a larger company can be difficult. Veritas said it would invest 8 million dollars over three years to expand the Dublin team.

To present the results of a research study
To recruit employees for a start-up
questions.explanation: It announces that Veritas has agreed to acquire Dunmore Data.

questions.explanation: The value of the transaction was not disclosed; the other points are covered.

documents.title: SkyBridge Airlines: Baggage allowance
documents.text:
Economy passengers may bring one cabin bag (maximum 8 kg, 55 x 40 x 20 cm) and one personal item that fits under the seat. A checked bag of up to 23 kg is included on international routes but not on domestic ones, where it costs 25 dollars if added online at least 24 hours before departure and 40 dollars at the airport. Business class passengers receive two checked bags of 32 kg each.

Sports equipment such as bicycles and skis counts as a checked bag, provided it is packed in a protective case; the fee is 60 dollars per item on all routes. Musical instruments smaller than a cello may travel in the cabin if they fit in the overhead locker. Larger instruments require an additional seat to be purchased.

Liquids in the cabin are limited to 100 ml per container. Items exceeding the allowance will be charged at 15 dollars per kilogram at the airport. Passengers traveling with infants may bring a stroller and a car seat free of charge in addition to their allowance. To avoid delays, please check the size of your cabin bag using the gauge at the gate before boarding.

documents.title: Question about baggage
documents.text:
Dear SkyBridge,

I am booked on flight SB 218 from Chicago to Denver on 14 May in economy. I intend to bring a suitcase weighing about 20 kg and my violin, which is in a standard case. I have not yet added any baggage online. Also, my colleague is bringing a folding bicycle in a hard case. Could you confirm what we would need to pay and whether the violin can be taken into the cabin?

Thank you,
Yuki Tanabe

documents.title: Re: Question about baggage
documents.text:
Dear Ms. Tanabe,

Flight SB 218 is a domestic service, so the 23 kg bag is not included. If you add it online by 13 May, you pay 25 dollars; otherwise 40 dollars at the airport. Your violin may be carried in the cabin, as long as it fits in the overhead locker, so you will not pay for it. Your colleague's bicycle counts as a checked bag, and the fee is 60 dollars per item, regardless of the route.

Please note that if your suitcase turns out heavier than 23 kg, 15 dollars is charged for each additional kilogram. Safe travels.

Regards,
Customer Support

documents.title: Letter to tenants about rent adjustment
documents.text:
Dear Tenant,

I am writing on behalf of Redfern Property Management to inform you of an adjustment to the rent for your apartment at Marlowe Court, which will take effect on 1 January. Under the terms of your lease, rents may be reviewed once a year in line with the regional index of housing costs. This year the index has risen by 3.8 percent, and the owners have decided to apply an increase of 3 percent, which is below the permitted level.

Your new monthly rent will be shown on the attached statement. If you pay by standing order, please note that you will need to update the amount with your bank by 15 December; the management company will not do this on your behalf. Tenants who have lived in their apartment for more than five years will receive a one-time credit of 100 dollars toward the January payment in recognition of their loyalty.

In the coming spring, the owners also intend to replace the elevators, a project that is expected to take three months. We will give you at least four weeks' notice before work begins, and we will arrange for a temporary service for residents with limited mobility. If you have any questions, you are welcome to attend a residents' meeting in the lobby on 27 November at 6:30 p.m.

Yours faithfully,
Leila Mansour, Property Manager

choices: To invite the tenants to move out of their apartments
To announce the sale of the whole building shortly
To remind the tenants to pay their overdue rent
To tell tenants about a change in housing costs
questions.explanation: It informs tenants of the rent increase and related matters.

choices: A single reduction on their next payment

questions.explanation: The rise applied is below the level that the lease allows.

documents.title: Exhibition review: "Salt and Light" at the Corvin Gallery
documents.text:
The Corvin Gallery's new exhibition, devoted to the coastal photography of the late Marta Illes, is at once a triumph of curation and a missed opportunity. The first three rooms are superb. Hung with unusual restraint, the black-and-white prints of fishing villages gain a quiet power from the generous spacing; each image seems to wait for the viewer rather than demand attention. The wall texts are brief and informative, resisting the temptation to explain what is already visible.

The fourth room is where the show falters. Here, the curators have added a looping video of waves with a soundtrack of recorded interviews, presumably to bring Illes's world to life. In practice, the audio spills into the adjoining space and distracts from the prints, which are, in any case, the artist's real achievement. [A] The final room, containing her little-known color work from the 1980s, deserves a larger audience; it is tucked away behind the gift shop and can easily be missed. [B]

For visitors, a few practical notes. Admission is 12 dollars, free on the first Sunday of the month, and the exhibition runs until 3 March. The catalog, at 38 dollars, is handsomely produced but contains few of the color images, which seems a pity. Overall, the show is worth a visit, ideally on a quiet weekday morning, when the silence suits the work.

questions.prompt: What is the reviewer's overall opinion?
choices: Strongly negative because of the high admission prices
Completely positive without any reservation at all
Unable to decide because of the poor lighting
Mostly positive, with some criticism of later rooms
questions.explanation: The reviewer praises the first rooms and objects to the video and the hidden final room, but still recommends a visit.

questions.prompt: What criticism is made of the fourth room?
choices: The prints are hung too close to one another
Noise from the video disturbs other parts of the show
The wall texts explain far too much about the images
The room is too dark for visitors to see the pictures
questions.explanation: The audio spills into the adjoining space and distracts from the prints.

questions.prompt: What can be inferred about the color photographs?
choices: They were taken after the photographer's death
They are less famous than her black-and-white work
They are all reproduced in the exhibition catalog
They are displayed in the first room of the gallery
questions.explanation: The review calls them 'little-known' work and says they are tucked away.

questions.prompt: In which position marked [A], [B], [C] or [D] does the following sentence best belong? "A quieter presentation of the interviews, perhaps on headphones, would have solved the problem."
questions.explanation: The sentence offers a remedy for the audio problem that has just been described, so it fits at [A] immediately after the criticism of the distracting sound.

documents.title: Notice: Changes to the Harbor Ferry timetable
documents.text:
From Monday 2 March, the Harbor Ferry will operate a revised winter timetable. Departures from the Eastside terminal will leave at 6:45, 7:30 and 8:15 a.m., then hourly from 9:00 a.m. until 4:00 p.m., and at 5:15 and 6:00 p.m. The crossing takes twenty-five minutes. Because of low demand, there will be no service after 6:00 p.m. on weekdays, and weekend departures will begin at 9:00 a.m.

Season ticket holders may use their existing passes until their expiration date. The single fare increases from 3.20 to 3.60 dollars, while the monthly pass rises from 78 to 84 dollars. Bicycles may be carried free outside peak hours (7:00 to 9:00 a.m. and 4:30 to 6:30 p.m.).

documents.title: Complaint about the new timetable
documents.text:
Dear Harbor Ferry,

I read the notice about the new schedule with dismay. I work at the Westside hospital and finish my shift at 7:30 p.m. on weekdays, and until now I have been able to return on the 8:00 p.m. ferry. With no service after 6:00 p.m., I would have to take a bus that takes more than an hour. I also use a monthly pass, and I would like to know whether the price change affects me immediately.

I do not understand why a service so important to health workers is being reduced.

Mateo Ruiz

documents.title: Re: Complaint about the new timetable
documents.text:
Dear Mr. Ruiz,

Thank you for your message. We understand the difficulty for people working late shifts. Our passenger counts showed fewer than ten people per evening on the 8:00 p.m. sailing, but after your message and those of other hospital staff, the operator will examine a late departure at 7:45 p.m. on weekdays. The decision will be announced by 20 February, before the new timetable begins.

Your pass is valid until its end date, so you would pay the new price of 84 dollars only at renewal. In the meantime, a bus line 12 stops opposite the hospital, but we accept that this is not a satisfactory solution.

Sincerely,
Customer Relations

documents.title: Retail returns: updated procedure
documents.text:
To: Store managers
From: Fiona Garrity, Customer Experience
Date: 5 October

Effective 1 November, the return period for most products will be extended from 14 to 30 days. The decision follows a customer survey in which 62 percent of respondents named the short return window as their main frustration. The only exceptions are underwear, perishable goods and personalized items, which cannot be returned unless faulty.

Staff should continue to ask for a receipt, but a purchase can now be traced through the loyalty card or the payment card used. Where no proof of purchase is available, the item may be exchanged but not refunded, and store credit should be issued at the lowest price at which the item has been sold in the past ninety days. Refunds must always be made to the original payment method; cash refunds above 50 dollars require manager approval.

Managers are asked to brief their teams before 25 October and to display the new poster by the entrance. Training materials will be sent next week. Please note that during the first month, we will monitor the number of returns closely, since the longer period may increase them; a review will take place in December.

choices: A new refund method that applies to cash payments

A ban on any returns made without a receipt

questions.explanation: The return period is extended from 14 to 30 days.

choices: Give a full refund in cash

questions.explanation: Items may be exchanged but not refunded, with store credit at the lowest recent price.

questions.explanation: The memo says the longer period may increase returns and will be monitored.

documents.title: Invitation to speak at the Annual Safety Forum
documents.text:
Dear Dr. Mbeki,

On behalf of the Northern Industrial Safety Association, I am delighted to invite you to give a keynote address at our Annual Safety Forum on 11 November at the Clarendon Conference Center. Your recent study on fatigue and workplace accidents has generated considerable interest among our members, many of whom manage shift-based operations in manufacturing and mining.

We would be grateful if you could speak for forty-five minutes, followed by fifteen minutes for questions. The session would take place at 9:30 a.m. on the first day, immediately after the welcome address. We are able to offer an honorarium of 1,500 dollars and to cover your travel and one night's accommodation. Should you wish to bring a colleague to assist with the presentation, we could include a second registration at no charge.

The forum usually attracts around 400 delegates, and we will record the sessions for later distribution to members, unless you prefer otherwise. We would be happy to discuss any particular requirements for the technical setup. If you are able to accept, please confirm by 30 September, so that we can include your name in the printed program, which goes to press on 5 October.

With best regards,
Hannah Lowell, Program Chair

documents.title: Re: Invitation
documents.text:
Dear Ms. Lowell,

Thank you for the kind invitation, which I am pleased to accept. I should point out that I am committed to a project in Nairobi until 8 November and will land in the country on the morning of the 10th, so I would prefer not to stay overnight beforehand. I would also appreciate it if my talk were scheduled in the afternoon in case of flight delays. Regarding the recording, I would be glad to have it shared with members, provided that the slides containing unpublished data are removed.

My colleague, Dr. Sipho Dlamini, would join me for the question session.

Kind regards,
Dr. Amara Mbeki
